Top Stock Market Highlights of the Week: Anthropic, Frasers Property and Asean Digital Payments
article:
Welcome to this week’s edition of top stock market highlights.
This week, a frontier artificial intelligence (AI) lab made the largest market debut on record, while a court ruling cleared the way for a major Orchard Road redevelopment.
In Manila, Singapore also pitched deeper digital and energy ties across Asean.
A frontier AI lab makes a record-breaking market debut
Anthropic PBC
(NASDAQ: ANT) and its seven co-founders raised US$107.3 billion in an upsized initial public offering (IPO) and private placement, the company confirmed on 18 November 2026.
Anthropic sold 956.4 million shares and the co-founders another 23.6 million, all at US$83 each, above the marketed range of US$70 to US$78.
The pricing gives the maker of the Claude chatbot a fully diluted valuation of roughly US$1.5 trillion, placing it among the 15 largest listed companies by market value.
At US$81.3 billion, the IPO alone overtakes the US$75 billion listing by
Space Exploration Technologies Corp.
(NASDAQ: SPCX), or
SpaceX
, as the largest on record.
The remaining US$26 billion comes from a private placement with participants including Google, a unit of
Alphabet Inc
(NASDAQ: GOOGL),
Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.
(NASDAQ: AMD) and
Microsoft Corporation
(NASDAQ: MSFT).
NVIDIA Corporation
(NASDAQ: NVDA) is set to buy US$10 billion of shares in the placement.
Demand was strong, with orders nearing seven times the shares available, Bloomberg News reported.
There is a Singapore link, too.
Sovereign wealth fund GIC co-led Anthropic’s US$30 billion Series G round with Coatue in February 2026 at a US$380 billion post-money valuation, having also invested in the earlier Series F round.
Chief executive officer Dario Amodei said the best advice he had received during the process was: “Never let your company be worth a single dollar more than it’s really worth.”
The shares began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on 19 November 2026 (US time).
Court ruling clears the way for an Orchard Road redevelopment
Frasers Property Limited
(SGX: TQ5) is a step closer to consolidating a prime Orchard Road site after the High Court granted a sale order on 19 November 2026 for the collective sale of The Centrepoint’s rear block.
Frasers
won the tender on 27 February 2026 with a S$391.9 million bid, about 6.2% below the S$418 million guide price.
The deal hit a snag in August 2026, when the Strata Titles Board issued a stop order after two objections were not withdrawn during mediation.
The collective sale committee then applied to the High Court, and both objections were withdrawn before the hearing.
The leasehold rear block holds 66 apartments and 66 retail units, with around 52 years left on its 99-year lease.
Frasers reportedly already held all the retail strata units and eight apartments, or about 85% of the block’s share value.
It also owns about 96% of the freehold front block, which houses 151 retail units.
Completion will give Frasers full ownership of the rear block.
The group also owns the neighbouring 51 Cuppage Road office building and bought the adjacent Cuppage Terrace for S$175 million in August 2026.
It could potentially amalgamate the sites to tap the Urban Redevelopment Authority’s Strategic Development Incentive Scheme, which encourages more intensive redevelopment of ageing properties in key areas.
Singapore pitches a region-wide payment network for Asean
Prime Minister Lawrence Wong called on Asean to develop a region-wide network of cross-border payment systems on 15 November 2026, the opening day of the 49th Asean Summit in Manila.
He pointed to Singapore’s existing bilateral payment links with countries such as Malaysia and Thailand as a foundation.
Such a network would “make it easier and cheaper for our businesses and citizens to transact with one another”, benefiting tourists and those sending remittances home, he said.
These links include PayNow-PromptPay with Thailand, launched in 2021, and PayNow-DuitNow with Malaysia, launched in November 2023.
DBS Group Holdings Ltd
(SGX: D05),
Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation Limited
(SGX: O39) and
United Overseas Bank Limite
d (SGX: U11) were the
Singapore banks
taking part in the Thailand link at launch.
PM Wong also welcomed the signing of the Asean Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) on 14 November 2026, calling it a significant milestone, but said its real test would be in implementation.
On energy, he said the growing use of AI and other digital technologies would lift electricity demand in the region.
He urged member states to swiftly ratify the Asean Petroleum Security Agreement and prioritise the development of the Asean Power Grid.
Asean’s economies have grown by around 4% to 5% a year in recent years but have the potential to grow faster, PM Wong noted.
Singapore will assume the Asean chairmanship in 2027.
